work.text: He treats the widest range of subject, but he is most himself when depicting small figures in all sorts of garbs and poses … in his studies of Italian Vagabonds
work.lead: Arthur M. Hind, naming this set of beggars among Callot’s best:

source.author: Arthur M. Hind
source.title: A Short History of Engraving and Etching

moment.text: He also studied beggars and cripples more methodically than [Dürer, Brueghel], or Villamena, composing a natural history of mendicants … that was consulted by Rembrandt and all the Dutch.

source.author: A. Hyatt Mayor
source.title: Prints & People: A Social History of Printed Pictures
source.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: He made more than 1,400 etchings that chronicled the life of his period, featuring soldiers, clowns, drunkards, Romani, beggars, as well as court life.
